Nothing renders this file yet. `art` names the line-art symbol each card used; the symbols themselves, the stylesheet and the tints are in git history at the commit that removed projects/index.html.
intro: My collection of coded projects: backend, platform and frontend, usually where software meets awkward data, hardware limits or human workflows.

entries.title: Eater Restaurant Map
entries.description: 2,336 London restaurants, merged out of 296 scattered Eater guides. Installable, and self-hosted down to the vector tiles, so it still works offline on the Tube.

entries.title: Consultant Recruitment
entries.description: The NHS consultant-appointment process I used to run by hand, rebuilt as a typed seven-state workflow. 92.7% — EECS Final Year Project Prize.

entries.title: a3watch
entries.description: Home-server monitoring that never wakes a sleeping disk, names the process behind every spin-up, and meters its own electricity in pennies per year.

entries.title: Film Index
entries.description: A self-hosted cinema for the ~26,500 films of the TSPDT canon: catalogue, acquisition, and hardware-transcoded playback, on no runtime npm dependencies.

entries.title: Which? Archive
entries.description: 8,543 pages captured at a 100% rate, link-rewritten into a mirror that stands alone. A private archive of my own subscription; nothing republished.

entries.title: Immutable Media Vault
entries.description: A content-addressed archive built around one hard rule: never mutate the source. It refuses to run if Windows would update an access timestamp.

entries.title: Computer Science Work
entries.description: Seven assessed projects, history intact: 95.03% on CIFAR-10, 22.7M taxi trips on Spark, an XQuery corpus pipeline. Three graded 100%; the degree, 82.4%.

entries.title: paperWiz
entries.description: Per-monitor wallpapers colour-matched from one image — its own pywal palette engine, a hand-written COM projection, three languages in five years.

entries.title: cs-stats
entries.description: A browser-to-Streamlit pipeline that settled a friend-group CS2 leaderboard — normalised per round, so playing twice as much doesn't read as playing twice as well.

entries.title: Homelab Platform
entries.description: One outbound tunnel and one label-gated updater behind every private app. Push to main, live in two minutes, no open inbound ports.

entries.title: This Site
entries.description: Hand-written, dependency-free and designed to print as a CV. Carousel physics, theming and lazy loading, all implemented rather than imported — with 53 photographs brought down from 250 MB of originals to 5.7 MB served.
